quarterly_data.quarter: ASUS press release: Building ASUS for the Next Chapter of AI: Reflections from (08-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: ASUS Co-CEO S.Y. Hsu (company blog on his Bloomberg TV interview after the Q2 results): the server business 'grew around 200% YoY and approximately 58% QoQ in the second quarter'. At the beginning of the year ASUS targeted full-year AI server business growth of between 50% and 100%; given the strong momentum he is 'now confident we can achieve around 150% growth for the full year'. AI server visibility remains strong, supported by continued demand for compute infrastructure.
quarterly_data.figure: server business ~200% YoY, ~58% QoQ in Q2; FY AI server growth target raised from 50%-100% to ~150%

quarterly_data.quarter: ASUS press release: Building ASUS for the Next Chapter of AI: Reflections from (08-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Co-CEO S.Y. Hsu: ASUS is 'in the first wave of mass production on the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform', and order visibility across neocloud customers, large enterprises, research institutions and government-led sovereign AI programs 'extends well into 2027'. He sees three engines for next year: AI servers and infrastructure, premium PCs driven by the AI PC upgrade cycle, and AI applications and services (including sovereign AI infrastructure through Taiwan AI Cloud). He cites the ASUS AI POD on Vera Rubin as an example of landing in the first wave of a new platform (company claim).
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure (Vera Rubin mass production under way; order visibility well into 2027)

quarterly_data.quarter: ASUS press release: Building ASUS for the Next Chapter of AI: Reflections from (08-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Co-CEO S.Y. Hsu on the memory shortage: he does not think memory and chip shortages will ease quickly and said the constraints 'could continue until the end of 2028', because of strong AI server demand and memory makers prioritising AI and data center requirements over consumer markets; new capacity takes time. ASUS has responded by building strategic inventory, locking in long-term supplier agreements, designing flexibility across configurations and prioritising higher-value products, and has adjusted prices on some lines.
quarterly_data.figure: shortage could last until end of 2028 (management view)
